extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, Administrative Patent Judges (APJs), and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) engaged in PTAB/ex parte appeal practice
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing Board decisions on ex parte appeals, remands (for amendment, affidavits, or search), new grounds of rejection, rehearing, timing/deadlines, public access, and follow-on examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no obligation resting on the Board to consider new or amended claims submitted while it has jurisdiction of the appeal. However, a proposed amendment filed after the date of filing of a brief to either cancel claims (where cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim), or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form may be remanded for consideration by the examiner. If the proposed amendment is in effect an abandonment of the appeal, the appeal will normally be dismissed by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1206. Board may remand for limited classes of post-brief amendments; amendments that abandon the appeal generally result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to consider affidavits or declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations filed with the filing of a notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to the Board will be considered for entry only if the appellant makes the necessary showing under 37 CFR 1.116(e) as to why they are necessary and were not earlier presented. Affidavits or declarations filed after a final rejection and prior to a notice of appeal are handled as provided in MPEP §§715.09, 716, and 716.01. If such evidence has not been treated by the examiner, the Board or the Director may remand the proceeding to permit the examiner to consider such evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits filed after notice of appeal but before Board jurisdiction: examiner lacks authority to consider them unless the affidavit overcomes all rejections on appeal and a showing of good and sufficient reasons for late presentation is made. Affidavits offered with a rehearing request where no 41.50(b) rejection exists are usually not remanded and are considered only as arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by the Board for further search - rarity and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be extremely rare for the Board to remand a case to the examiner for further search. A remand to the examiner extends the total pendency of an application and may necessitate an extension of the patent term under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). When such a remand is necessary, the Board should conduct a search (on-line or otherwise) of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate the basis on which it concludes that a search of this area would be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cited art need not be art upon which a rejection can be made; remands for search should be justified and sparingly used because of pendency/term effects. See MPEP §2710 for patent term considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require additional briefing (37 CFR 41.50(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to additionally brief any matter that the Board considers to be of assistance in reaching a reasoned decision on the pending appeal. Appellant will be given a time period within which to respond to such an order. Failure to timely comply with the order may result in the sua sponte dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include applicability of particular case law or prior art not previously identified. Extensions of time for responding are only available under 37 CFR 1.136(b). Information disclosure statements filed while the Board has jurisdiction are held in abeyance until the Board's jurisdiction ends (see 37 CFR 41.35(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision options: affirm, reverse, remand (37 CFR 41.50(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, in its decision, may affirm or reverse the decision of the examiner in whole or in part on the grounds and on the claims specified by the examiner. The Board may also remand an application to the examiner. The affirmance of a rejection on any of the grounds specified constitutes a general affirmance except as to any ground specifically reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a substitute examiner's answer follows a remand, appellant must within two months either reopen prosecution (request prosecution be reopened under §1.111) or maintain the appeal (file a reply brief under §41.41). Actions taken affect whether the appeal is withdrawn/maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection by the Board (designation required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the Board have knowledge of any grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include in its opinion a statement to that effect with its reasons for so holding, and designate such a statement as a new ground of rejection of the claim. A new ground of rejection pursuant to this paragraph shall not be considered final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board designates a new ground, the appellant has two months to either (1) reopen prosecution by submitting appropriate amendment/new evidence (remand to examiner), or (2) request rehearing addressing the new ground and stating with particularity the points misapprehended or overlooked. If the new ground is undesignated, the remedy is rehearing under §41.52; failure to timely seek rehearing waives that argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after a Board-designated new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.50(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new ground of rejection is designated, within two months appellant must either (1) reopen prosecution by submitting an appropriate amendment and/or new evidence and have the matter reconsidered by the examiner (prosecution remanded), or (2) request rehearing by the Board upon the same record addressing the new ground with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appropriate amendment must amend rejected claims or substitute new claims directed to the same subject matter. New claims that merely add claims without amending/substituting rejected claims are not appropriate and will not be entered. New evidence may be a showing under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132. Time limits: 2 months; extensions only per 1.136(b) or 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes an 'appropriate amendment' under 41.50(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is 'appropriate' if it amends one or more of the claims rejected, or substitutes new claims to avoid the art or reasons adduced by the Board. Such amended or new claims must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims. An amendment which adds new claims without either amending the rejected claims or substituting new claims for the rejected claims is not appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a purported new claim contains argument concerning the Board’s rejection, the entry should be changed to a request for rehearing and examiner should consult a supervisor. New evidence can be showings under 1.130/1.131/1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument-only submissions after new ground treated as rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant submits an argument without either an appropriate amendment or new evidence as to any of the claims rejected by the Board, it will be treated as a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treating argument-only submissions as rehearing waives the right to limited prosecution under 41.50(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial amendment + rehearing handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant files an appropriate amendment/new evidence as to less than all claims rejected under 41.50(b), and requests rehearing as to the remainder, the examiner will not consider the claims for which rehearing was requested. The request for rehearing will be considered by the Board after prosecution with respect to the first group of claims is terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument as to claims rejected by the Board not accompanied by appropriate amendment/new evidence will be treated as a request for rehearing as to those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for responses to Board decisions and new grounds (2-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment and/or new evidence under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(1), or the request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(2), must be filed within 2 months from the date of the Board’s decision. In accordance with 37 CFR 41.50(f), this 2-month time period may not be extended by filing a petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a), but only under 37 CFR 1.136(b), or under 37 CFR 1.550(c) if in ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under §1.136(a) are not applicable to these time periods; use §1.136(b) or §1.550(c) where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing requirements and limitations (37 CFR 41.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the date of the original decision. The request must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board. Arguments not raised and evidence not previously relied upon pursuant to §§41.37, 41.41, or 41.47 are not permitted in the request for rehearing except as permitted by specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted new arguments: (A) based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision, (B) responding to a new ground of rejection under §41.50(b), (C) arguing the Board’s decision contains an undesignated new ground. Rehearing is normally on the written record; another oral hearing is not guaranteed. Two-month deadline extendable only under §1.136(b) or §1.550(c). If timely rehearing filed, the 63-day appeal/civil action period runs from decision on rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing is restricted to points misapprehended or overlooked
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for rehearing must be limited to the points of law or fact which appellant feels were overlooked or misapprehended by the Board. Experience has shown many rehearings are mere reargument; rules were revised to prohibit reargument except the narrow exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant relies on a recent relevant decision, the Board may remand to the examiner to respond to the new argument. New evidence not previously relied upon is generally barred in rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access to Board decisions (37 CFR 41.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Board action is available for public inspection without a party’s permission if rendered in a file open to the public pursuant to §1.11 or in an application published under §§1.211–1.221. The Office may independently publish any Board action that is available for public inspection. Actions not otherwise publishable may be published if the Director believes special circumstances warrant publication and the affected party does not timely object on trade-secret/confidential-information grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the action discloses confidential information, the party must identify necessary deletions and can seek reconsideration and court review before contested portions are made public. Records of proceedings are available unless the application is not otherwise public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure following Board decision: jurisdiction and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, jurisdiction over an application or patent under ex parte reexamination proceeding passes to the examiner, subject to appellant's right of appeal or other review, for such further action as may be required to carry the decision into effect. The 63-day period for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action or the two-month period for filing a request for rehearing begins to run from the 'mail date' (paper) or 'notification date' (electronic) shown on FORM PTOL-90A attached to the decision. If Board decision affirms or affirms in part the examiner, the examiner must await expiration of the two-month period before taking further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Palpable administrative timing: the application is returned to the Technology Center electronically by changing PALM status code reflecting the Board decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board remand not a final action for judicial review (37 CFR 41.50(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a decision of the Board includes a remand, that decision shall not be considered final for judicial review. After conclusion of proceedings on remand before the examiner, the Board may enter an order making its decision final for judicial review as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate and judicial review consequences differ when a remand is involved; finality is delayed until Board acts after remand if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when examiner is reversed in whole
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reversal of the examiner’s rejection brings the case up for immediate action by the examiner. The examiner should not regard such a reversal as a challenge to make a new search to uncover other and better references; the second examiner should give full faith and credit to the prior examiner’s search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner has specific knowledge of references indicating nonpatentability of appealed claims, they should submit the matter to the TC Director or CRU Director for authorization to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.198; such requests for rehearing by the examiner must state with particularity points misapprehended and are limited to new arguments based on recent relevant decisions. All examiner rehearing requests require approval by the TC/CRU Director and Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy before mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims not appealed (withdrawn claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 41.31(c), an appeal is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims. Where, in an appeal brief filed before January 23, 2012, an appellant withdraws some appealed claims (i.e., claims subject to a ground of rejection that the appellant did not present for review in the brief), and the Board reverses on the remaining appealed claims, the withdrawal is treated as authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must notify the appellant of the cancellation of the withdrawn claims. See MPEP §1205.02 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on extensions of time for appeal-related deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under §1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the time periods set forth in these sections (e.g., the 2-month and 63-day periods). See §1.136(b) for extensions to reply for patent applications and §1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the mechanisms specifically identified (1.136(b), 1.550(c)) may be used to extend appeal-related deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of undesignated new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of a panel's failure to designate a new ground of rejection in its decision must be raised by filing a request for rehearing as set forth in §41.52. Failure of appellant to timely file such a request for rehearing will constitute a waiver of any arguments that a decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely rehearing is the exclusive route to challenge an undesignated new ground; rehearing must comply with the particularity requirement and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if examiner sustains rejections in whole or in part
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is sustained in whole or in part and claims require action, proceedings may be considered terminated in certain circumstances (e.g., dismissal of appeal), but where claims are allowed or the nature of the decision requires further action by the examiner, prosecution continues as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.35 for jurisdictional end points; examiner must follow applicable MPEP guidance (e.g., §1214.06) when further action is required.
